description: order.py has NO independent, hard-coded ceiling on the order size it will submit to the CLOB. It fully trusts the `size_usdc` argument passed in from decide.py/run.sh (order.py:37,71-72) with zero defense-in-depth cap. decide.py's own caps (lib.position_size max_bet_pct=0.05, lib.risk_gate daily/drawdown caps) are all proportional to a caller-supplied `bankroll` (decide.py:139 reads PM_BANKROLL env or argv[1], default 8) -- if that env var or argv is ever misconfigured/too large in the calling context (cron/launchd), the computed stake scales with it and order.py will post it unquestioned. There is also no validation that `price` is within (0,1) or that computed `shares` is above the exchange's minimum order size before calling create_and_post_order (order.py:71-72) -- a price of 0 raises an uncaught ZeroDivisionError (crash, no order, but ungraceful) while a tiny/zero size is passed straight through to the live endpoint.
